comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Physics
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 current programme and course records; official 180-EC structure checked 2026-10-06
comparator.sourceNotes: The current TU/e programme and degree-structure material identifies a three-year, 180-EC Applied Physics bachelor. The governing Bachelor College directive accounts for the whole degree as a 125-EC core, including a 10-, 15- or 20-EC Bachelor Final Project, 45 EC of elective space and 10 EC of Impact of Technology. Current 2026-2027 course records substantiate the programme-specific cumulative formation in mathematical physics, mechanics and dynamical systems, electromagnetism and optics, thermal and quantum physics, programming, data acquisition, laboratory practice, advanced computational and experimental research skills and a concluding Applied Physics project. No named route or specialisation is required for the normalized target, and genuine elective space is preserved rather than populated with invented choices.

programmes.label: Bachelor Applied Physics at Eindhoven University of Technology

exception.reason: Applied Physics at TU/e is a cumulative physics-and-engineering degree whose compulsory core integrates mathematical modelling and programming with mechanics and nonlinear dynamics, electromagnetism and optics, thermodynamics, quantum and materials physics, experimental design, data acquisition, measurement and error analysis, laboratory practice, advanced computational and experimental research skills and a discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers a useful mathematics and computational-modelling sequence and two broad sustainability gateways that touch selected physical concepts, but it does not offer the university-level physics theory sequence, experimental-physics laboratory and instrumentation progression, quantum and materials sequence, or comparable applied-physics research environment needed to preserve the target's academic identity. A 24-course UCR pathway could study mathematical modelling and technology in an interdisciplinary way, but it would not be a defensible Applied Physics comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official structure accounts for the full 180 EC as a 125-EC Applied Physics core including the Bachelor Final Project, 45 EC of genuine elective space and 10 EC of Impact of Technology. Current course records for the 2026 academic catalogue substantiate a connected progression from introductory applied physics, calculus, linear algebra and programming through mechanics, optics, data acquisition and processing and quantum physics to advanced experimental and computational research work. The current records make explicit the use of differential equations and nonlinear dynamics, Maxwell's equations and light-matter interaction, the Schrödinger equation, experimental design, scientific hardware, uncertainty analysis and independent research practice. These are not isolated electives but mutually supporting elements of a physics degree.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide meaningful mathematical foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science add computational foundations, while DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision offers general digital image analysis. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I surveys selected concepts from physics, chemistry and materials science in a sustainability context, and ENSGATE201 Sustainability Essentials II includes broad work on waves, chemistry and materials. The workbook nevertheless contains no dedicated classical and advanced mechanics sequence, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, optics, wave physics, physical transport phenomena, solid-state or materials physics, circuits and electronics, scientific instrumentation, precision measurement, or cumulative experimental-physics laboratory sequence. DISMATH312 studies mathematical systems, differential equations and signal representations rather than physical electronics and measurement hardware; DISDATA212 studies image-processing algorithms rather than imaging physics or instrument design; and the sustainability gateways introduce selected concepts for environmental study rather than forming a physics sequence. UCR also lacks TU/e's staged applied-physics challenge and laboratory work, advanced experimental research course and discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. The closest possible 24-course UCR combination would therefore be a mathematical and sustainability-oriented liberal-arts pathway with the target programme's defining physical theory, experimentation and engineering formation absent.
